title: Dairy Valley Paneer Launches in Sainsbury’s and Tesco After Historic Cheese Awards Gold
excerpt: The first paneer ever to win Gold at the International Cheese & Dairy Awards goes on sale in Sainsbury’s next week, with Tesco in November — paneer’s big mainstream-UK moment.
body:
• Golden Acre Foods is launching Dairy Valley Paneer — the first paneer ever to win Gold at the International Cheese & Dairy Awards — in Sainsbury’s stores nationwide next week at £3.50 per 200g pack, with Tesco following in November.
  • The paneer is made in Bulgaria by Indian chef Bipen Sharma, who set out to reproduce the soft texture and clean taste of Indian paneer rather than a Westernized imitation.
  • Rebecca Cutter, Golden Acre’s marketing director, said the Gold award “recognised the product’s quality and authenticity” and the listings advance the company’s push into authentic world foods at major retailers.
  • The launch moves paneer from South Asian independent grocers into mainstream UK retail — billed in the trade as “the new halloumi.”

Paneer is having a moment in Britain — and now it has the medal to prove it. Dairy Valley Paneer, the first paneer ever to win Gold at the International Cheese & Dairy Awards, is launching into Sainsbury’s stores nationwide next week at £3.50 per 200g pack, with a Tesco listing following in November 2026.

The launch is the work of Golden Acre Foods, the UK’s leading world-foods distributor, founded in 1999 and based in Chertsey, Surrey. The company sources from more than 10 countries, supplies all four of Britain’s biggest supermarket chains, and is B Corp certified. Its marketing director, Rebecca Cutter, said the listings are part of a broader strategy to expand authentic world-food products through major UK retailers and respond to demand for Indian ingredients.

“The taste of Bharat reaching plates around the world.”

— Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mann Ki Baat, April 2026

The chef behind it

Dairy Valley Paneer is made by Indian chef Bipen Sharma, who founded the Dairy Valley brand. Sharma set out to reproduce the taste, appearance and texture of Indian paneer outside India — not a Westernized imitation. He chose a European production base in Bulgaria, where he says local cows’ milk closely matches the milk of Indian cows, yielding the soft texture and clean taste of South Asian paneer. The result can be spread or crumbled into dishes.

The International Cheese & Dairy Awards is one of the world’s major dairy competitions — its 2026 schedule ran at the Staffordshire County Showground in June — and no paneer had previously taken its top Gold medal. The historic win gave Golden Acre the retail story it needed: an award the buyers could not ignore.

“The new halloumi”

For years, paneer in Britain was a staple bought at South Asian independent grocers — familiar to Indian households, unknown to most everyone else. That is changing. The trade now bills paneer as “the new halloumi,” and the numbers back the push: Mintel’s UK World Cuisines Report 2023 found 92% of Brits ate world cuisines at home within three months.

Indian cheese on the global stage is on a roll. At the 2026 Mundial do Queijo do Brasil, Indian cheesemakers Eleftheria Cheese of Mumbai and Nordic Farm of Ladakh won a Super Gold, two Golds and a Silver on their international debut — a haul Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed in his April 2026 Mann Ki Baat address as “the taste of Bharat reaching plates around the world.”

For Britain’s large Indian community, the appeal is simpler: paneer that tastes like home, finally on the shelf next to the cheddar.
